_description: Structured feature tags for rule-based case matching in Agent 3 analysis. v2.4 adds ruling_logic per case for L2 logic-level matching.
_matching_logic: Agent 3 builds a case_profile from the current case, then matches against these tags. L1: exact match on violation_type + subject_level = high relevance. L2: ruling_logic matching via core_principle similarity. L3: difference analysis via not_applicable_when.

cases.name: Official Vehicle Misuse / Private Vehicle Using Public Funds
cases.violation_type: Integrity Discipline - Violation of Eight-point Regulation + Embezzlement (Wind-to-Corruption)
cases.mental_state: Knowing and willful - Intent to unlawfully possess
cases.penalty: Serious Party Internal Warning + Administrative Demotion
cases.key_ruling: Official vehicle for personal use = conduct issue (minor); Private vehicle using public funds = corruption issue (severe) - Distinguishing 'conduct' from 'corruption'

ruling_logic.core_principle: Distinguishing 'conduct issues' from 'corruption' — different stages in the same behavioral chain may violate different categories of discipline
distinction_criteria: Whether public funds entered personal pockets
Whether behavior is 'use' or 'appropriation'
Duration and frequency
ruling_logic.applicable_when: Public-private mixed-use scenarios, blurred cost boundaries, small amounts but long duration
ruling_logic.not_applicable_when: Purely personal consumption unrelated to official duties, amounts large enough to constitute embezzlement

cases.name: Fault Tolerance and Error Correction - Dual-Factor Analysis
cases.violation_type: Fault Tolerance and Error Correction Mechanism
cases.mental_state: Intent to promote development - No personal gain
cases.key_ruling: Violation does not equal disciplinary violation - Requires three-dimensional judgment of 'violation elements + culpability elements + exculpatory circumstances'

ruling_logic.core_principle: Three Distinctions — violation ≠ disciplinary breach; requires three-dimensional judgment: violation elements + culpability elements + exculpatory circumstances
distinction_criteria: Whether subjective purpose was to promote development or seek personal gain
Whether procedure was substantively compliant or merely form-deficient
Whether irreparable loss was caused
ruling_logic.applicable_when: Exploratory mistakes in reform and innovation, procedural deficiencies with substantive compliance, no personal benefit transfer
ruling_logic.not_applicable_when: Knowing and willful violations, using reform as a cover for disciplinary breaches, causing significant foreseeable losses

cases.name: Obstructing Organizational Investigation
cases.violation_type: Political Discipline - Obstructing Organizational Investigation + Bribe-Taking
cases.mental_state: Deliberate deception - Intent to obstruct investigation
cases.penalty: Expulsion from the Party + Dismissal from Public Office + Referral to Judicial Authorities
cases.key_ruling: Failure to truthfully respond during inquiry + collusion to fabricate evidence = collectively determined as obstructing organizational investigation (Political Discipline), not Organizational Discipline

ruling_logic.core_principle: Qualitative upgrade for resisting organizational review — collusion + evidence fabrication = political discipline violation, not organizational discipline
distinction_criteria: Whether there was active collusion
Whether substantive evidence was fabricated
Whether the timing was before or after organizational interview
ruling_logic.applicable_when: Collusion during organizational review, fabricating evidence materials, directing others to commit perjury
ruling_logic.not_applicable_when: Mere failure to truthfully explain, passive avoidance of questions, no fabrication

cases.name: Formalism and Bureaucratism
cases.violation_type: Violation of Eight-point Regulation - Formalism and Bureaucratism
cases.key_ruling: Formalism and Bureaucratism = violation of Eight-point Regulation, stated separately in adjudication documents. If consequences resulted, handle per regulations; if no consequences, apply First Form

ruling_logic.core_principle: Superficiality Identification for formalism/bureaucratism — distinguish 'unintentional error' from 'deliberate inaction', graded by consequences
distinction_criteria: Whether there were actual consequences
Whether it was capability deficiency or attitude problem
Whether isolated incident or long-term pattern
ruling_logic.applicable_when: Inaction without direct loss, typical form-over-substance behavior
ruling_logic.not_applicable_when: Caused severe and foreseeable consequences, underlying benefit transfer, systematic fraud

cases.name: Blank Official Letter Embezzlement
cases.violation_type: Integrity Discipline - Embezzlement (Blank Official Letter Reimbursement)
cases.penalty: Serious Party Internal Warning + Administrative Major Demerit
cases.key_ruling: Blank official letter reimbursement = embezzlement (not ordinary irregular dining). Distinguish personal embezzlement from collective violation

ruling_logic.core_principle: Seeing Through Appearance to Essence — blank official letter reimbursement appears to be 'improper reception' but is substantively 'embezzlement'. Distinguish individual misappropriation from collective violation
distinction_criteria: Whether funds entered personal pockets
Whether there were fabricated official activities
Whether it was systematic exploitation or individual forgery
ruling_logic.applicable_when: Obtaining public funds under false pretenses, multiple participants following the same pattern at different times
ruling_logic.not_applicable_when: Genuine official activities with only excessive amounts, no intent to misappropriate

cases.name: Irregular Dining with Mixed Public-Private Funds
cases.violation_type: Integrity Discipline - Irregular Public-Funded Dining (Mixed Public-Private)
cases.key_ruling: Mixed public-private banquets - split treatment: public-funded portion characterized as disciplinary violation + restitution; personal portion borne by participants themselves

ruling_logic.core_principle: Segmented treatment of public-private mixed scenarios — public-fund portion characterized separately + restitution; private portion handled independently. Do not characterize the entire event as a disciplinary violation merely because of partial public funding
distinction_criteria: Proportion of public funds
Who initiated
Whether participants knew public funds were used
ruling_logic.applicable_when: Group meals partially reimbursed with public funds, subordinates attending superior-initiated official banquets
ruling_logic.not_applicable_when: Fully public-funded with no official purpose, concealing personal consumption

cases.name: Illegal Levy of Fees
cases.violation_type: Mass Line Discipline - Illegal Levy of Fees
cases.penalty: Serious Party Internal Warning + Administrative Demotion
cases.key_ruling: Illegal levy of fees = infringement of public interests (Mass Line Discipline), not ordinary financial violation

ruling_logic.core_principle: Disciplinary characterization of improper levies — violation of Mass Discipline (infringing on the people's interests), not ordinary financial violation. Levying on managed service recipients is its defining feature
distinction_criteria: Whether levy targets are subordinate units or ordinary people
Whether official authority influence was involved
Whether expenses were for official or personal purposes
ruling_logic.applicable_when: Using official authority to levy on subordinate units or managed service recipients
ruling_logic.not_applicable_when: Normal internal cost allocation within an organization, no authority factor

cases.name: Irregular Handling of Wedding or Funeral Events
cases.violation_type: Integrity Discipline - Irregular Handling of Wedding or Funeral Events
cases.mental_state: Knowing and willful - Intent to collect money through events
cases.penalty: Party Internal Warning to Serious Warning
cases.key_ruling: No blanket prohibition - Key considerations: 'whether authority or position influence was leveraged' + 'whether adverse social impact was caused' + local economic and customary factors

ruling_logic.core_principle: Wedding/funeral events are 'not absolutely prohibited' — key tests: 'whether official authority influence was used' + 'whether adverse social impact was caused' + local economic and customary factors
distinction_criteria: Whether managed service recipients attended
Whether gift amounts significantly exceeded local norms
Whether events were staged in installments to evade regulation
ruling_logic.applicable_when: Managed service recipients attended, using official influence to receive clearly excessive gifts
ruling_logic.not_applicable_when: Only relatives attended, gift amounts within local norms, no authority factor

cases.name: Irregular Acceptance of Banquets After Retirement
cases.violation_type: Integrity Discipline - Irregular Acceptance of Banquets After Retirement
cases.key_ruling: Retirement does not equal immunity - Accepting banquets after retirement by leveraging former authority or position-established convenience conditions can still constitute a disciplinary violation

ruling_logic.core_principle: Retirement ≠ Immunity — using convenience formed by former official position or status can constitute a disciplinary violation even after retirement. Key test: 'whether former position influence persists'
distinction_criteria: Whether the favor request relates to former official duties
Time interval (how long after retirement)
Whether there was a clear 'helping' act
ruling_logic.applicable_when: Interacting with former managed service recipients shortly after retirement, favor requests directly related to former duties
ruling_logic.not_applicable_when: Normal social interaction years after retirement, no favor request, no connection to former position

cases.name: Simplistic and Overbroad Accountability
cases.key_ruling: Accountability cannot be 'one-size-fits-all' - Must distinguish direct responsibility / leadership responsibility; cannot pursue accountability for its own sake

ruling_logic.core_principle: Accountability must not be 'one-size-fits-all' — must distinguish direct responsibility / managerial responsibility / supervisory responsibility; must not pursue accountability for its own sake
distinction_criteria: Whether the person is the direct operator or manager
Whether there are clearly defined duty boundaries
Whether grassroots objective constraints were considered
ruling_logic.applicable_when: Multiple persons held accountable without distinguishing responsibility levels, grassroots cadres given maximum punishment without clear subjective fault
ruling_logic.not_applicable_when: Responsibility levels clearly distinguished, each level has clear dereliction of duty

cases.name: Fraudulently Obtaining Agricultural Subsidies
cases.violation_type: Mass Line Discipline - Fraudulent Subsidy Obtainment + Embezzlement
cases.penalty: Revocation of Party Position + Confiscation of Illegal Gains
cases.key_ruling: Grassroots cadre fraudulently obtaining agricultural subsidies = Mass Line Discipline + Embezzlement dual characterization. Village committee director recommended to resign from position

ruling_logic.core_principle: Dual characterization for grassroots cadres defrauding subsidies — Mass Discipline violation + Embezzlement. Village committee director should be recommended to resign (not subject to administrative sanctions)
distinction_criteria: Whether the subject is an administrative agency appointee
Whether the defrauded funds were state subsidies or collective funds
Whether the amount meets the criminal prosecution threshold
ruling_logic.applicable_when: Grassroots organization personnel using official convenience to defraud state subsidies
ruling_logic.not_applicable_when: Ordinary villagers without official convenience defrauding subsidies (not supervisory targets)
